apps.localizedDescription:
XeniOS is an Xbox 360 emulator for iPhone and iPad, based on Xenia.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later and JIT, enabled through StikDebug. See https://xenios.jp/download/ios for setup.

No games are included. Use only games you dumped from discs or digital purchases you own.

versions.localizedDescription:
Fixes on top of 2.3.1, a large round of graphics work, and Xenia Edge as of November 12. Games draw closer to the way an Xbox 360 draws them, and the app does less GPU and CPU work for each frame.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Fixes

- DLC is now installed so games can find it. DLC you installed before is moved to the new layout on first launch, and a move cut short by closing the app is finished on the next launch.
- Games that play sound through more than one audio stream (for example Left 4 Dead 2) are no longer silent, and their streams no longer stay silent after the audio engine has to be rebuilt.
- Draws that export memory now wait for their shaders to compile instead of being skipped. This fixes games freezing the first time those shaders compile, such as Battlefield 4.
- Draws that would leave a lasting mark if drawn with a stand-in shader (clears, draws that set depth or stencil in the pixel shader, draws a game issues only once) now wait for their own shader.
- Draws that ask the GPU for occlusion results no longer stop the game while a shader compiles.
- Stored shaders are kept where iOS doesn't empty them while the app is closed. The existing cache is moved there on first launch. From this version on, they also survive app updates that leave shader translation unchanged.
- A launch with stored shaders no longer translates every shader again. On a Mac, the Halo 3 menu's 102 shaders took about a quarter of a second to translate on each launch.
- Fixed a rare wrong frame in Halo 3 when a depth buffer was copied into a second color target.
- A settings file that can't be read no longer stops the app from starting. XeniOS keeps a backup of the last settings that loaded, sets the broken file aside as a copy, and asks at launch whether to restore the backup or reset to defaults. On a Mac it uses the backup, or the defaults, and shows a warning.
- A custom internal resolution outside the supported range in the settings file is reset instead of stopping the launch.
- Fixed the app freezing and being closed by iOS when System Link settings changed.
- Fixed a crash after closing the gamertag sheet while going online, renaming or checking a name.
- Fixed a crash on a game page after Create Private Room.
- Fixed a crash in the touch controls editor when selecting another control while dragging the opacity slider.
- Public Games now shows game names for games without a XeniOS compatibility report, instead of "Game" and a title ID.
- Mac: games keep their speed while XeniOS is in the background.
- A game deleted in the Files app no longer stays in the library, or in Convert to ZAR, while it waits in Recently Deleted.
- Mac: the window's volume slider and mute now work with the default audio driver. Before, they did nothing.
- Two discs of a game that carry the same disc number (Halo 3 and its Mythic disc are both "disc 1 of 1") are told apart by their file names, in the library and when converted to ZAR.

## Graphics

Closer to the console. Each of the first four was checked against the same tests run on an Xbox 360:

- Gamma render targets (8_8_8_8_GAMMA) are stored as the console's 8-bit gamma, and blending into them uses the console's arithmetic. Our nine gamma blend tests now match the console exactly.
- 16-bit fixed-point render targets (16_16 and 16_16_16_16) are encoded and blended with the console's arithmetic. In the 16_16_16_16 blend tests, the values that differ from the console dropped from thousands to tens.
- 2x and 4x MSAA resolves into 8-bit targets average their samples with the console's rounding.
- Resolves whose destination pitch isn't a multiple of 32 texels, or is narrower than the copied area, lay out their pixels as the console does.
- Float-to-integer conversions in shaders saturate as they do on the console, in every shader stage.
- Rectangles drawn with a zero W cover the whole scissor, sampler border colors take their alpha from the console's setting, and 16-bit index 0xFFFF is drawn as a vertex where the game leaves primitive restart on.

Less work per frame:

- Games that draw a frame in several strips, as Halo 3 does (1152x640 at 4x MSAA in four strips), are drawn in one go once XeniOS has verified that every strip draws the same thing. This now also covers frames with draws that appear in the first strip only, and strips that draw to another surface.
- Resolves of the common color formats run inside the open render pass, reading samples from tile memory instead of storing them and reading them back. Two textures of the same resolved memory share one image instead of being written twice.
- Clears drawn as full-screen quads no longer copy or load the render target contents they overwrite, and a render pass that begins by drawing over its whole area doesn't load the old contents.
- Render target copies that a game reads back on the CPU no longer hold up the GPU thread every frame. XeniOS waits only when the game actually reads that memory.
- A texture the game writes again with the same bytes isn't loaded again.
- Draws that can't change anything are skipped.
- Vertex shaders leave out the console-exact rounding steps in draws where the result is proven to be the same.
- Depth and 4x MSAA color render targets can stay losslessly compressed on Apple GPUs.
- Less CPU time in the GPU command processor: textures, descriptors and shaders are looked up again only when they change, and runs of no-op packets are skipped in one step.

## CPU and audio

- The audio worker and the frame limiter sleep until their deadline instead of spinning a CPU core. In gameplay on an iPhone the two were using about 84 ms of CPU time every second.
- The ARM64 recompiler checks floating-point results for NaN only where one can occur, and builds floating-point compare results from a single host compare.
- Fixed an ARM64 recompiler bug, present since 2.2, that stopped returns into dynamically generated code from being recognised. Halo 2, run through the console's original Xbox emulator, hung at boot on a Mac because of it.
- Branches in dynamically generated code to the address after a call are now resolved in recompiled code instead of by a call into the emulator. In a two and a half minute run of Halo 2 on a Mac, 395 million of 405 million such branches were resolved that way, each with the same result as the old path.

## Xenia Edge

XeniOS is an iOS and macOS app built on [Xenia Edge](https://github.com/has207/xenia-edge). The emulator work that isn't specific to iOS, including the ARM64 recompiler and the Metal renderer, is done together with that project. This release is up to date with Xenia Edge as of November 12, which brings:

- Games' own exception handlers now run. Access violations and calls to addresses with no code are delivered to the game as the console's kernel delivers them, with RtlUnwind and structured exception handling implemented.
- Virtual memory: allocations are checked against the game's reservations, unaligned ranges commit the right pages, and only newly committed pages are cleared.
- Threads and I/O: fixes for event waits, manual-reset events that lost waiters, I/O completion timeouts, and threads that exit with I/O pending.
- Audio: background music (XMP) plays through the audio driver. XMA no longer drops the frame after one that ends on a packet boundary.
- Graphics: YCbCr front buffers are supported, and the picture is cropped to the display scaler's source rectangle.
- CPU: PowerPC floating-point results and flags (NaN, FPSCR, XER overflow) and lwarx/stwcx reservations.
- Kernel: thread stacks are allocated as kernel stacks, placed by type and page size as on the console.
- Content: every content package volume reports as a hard drive, and XCTD-compressed files are reported as such.

## Improvements

- With no network connection (for example in Airplane Mode), the app no longer tries to reach the online service. Online screens say "No Internet Connection", and everything reconnects by itself when the connection returns. Local play and System Link on your local network still work.
- A profile the online service has stopped (refused, removed, or signed in on another device) keeps showing the reason when the network returns, instead of trying again.
- The online service now gets a device ID that stays the same when the app is deleted and installed again: a hash of a random value kept in the Keychain, or on a Mac a hash of the hardware ID. Device bans rely on it.
- Anonymous crash reports and statistics that couldn't be sent because the network dropped are sent when it returns.
- While stored shaders are rebuilt, the launch screen and the in-game shader indicator show that rebuild's own progress from the start, and stop when it is done. Before, the bar could run ahead, jump, or stay on "Preparing shaders" until the first frame.
- Crash reports say where in the game's code a crash happened and what led up to it: the last few events (game start, first frame, memory warnings, going to the background, heat), the game's version, and which emulation settings differ from their defaults.
- Compatibility data is checked once a day instead of every six hours.
- Notice text on the library is easier to read, and the profile page is more compact.
- Converting the whole library to ZAR shows how much space it saved.
- Settings has a Startup page under App, with Start with the Dashboard and Turn On JIT Automatically. They were under Advanced → Automation. The Turn On JIT sheet has the same switch for opening StikDebug automatically.
- Live Log is a dark console: each line is marked in its level's colour, it can be filtered to warnings or errors, and a Latest button returns to the end.

## New

- Storage, under Settings → Library & Storage. It shows what XeniOS uses by kind and by game, and for each game offers Clear Shaders, Delete Updates and Add-ons, Delete Saves and Delete Game. Clear Game Data, Clear All Shaders and Clean Up Leftover Files work on the whole app. Files left by games that are no longer in the library are listed too.
- Storage also sorts games by size or name, deletes several selected games together, and deletes one disc of a game that has several. Games in a linked folder on the device are counted as Linked Games; games linked from another drive are listed outside the total.
- Original Xbox games are listed in the library with their cover and name, as disc images, ZAR archives or extracted folders, and start through the Xbox 360's own Xbox emulator. Storage lists them in their own section. Experimental and slow: see Known issues.
- XeniOS doesn't include that Xbox emulator. System Software has an Original Xbox Games section that installs it from Files (the Compatibility folder from an Xbox 360's hard drive, the folder it is in, or its files), shows what is installed, and removes it. Start Games With chooses the build games start through: Automatic, where xbox.xex picks one for each game as the console does, or any installed build. A game's own Game Settings has Xbox Emulator Build to choose a different one for that game. Opening an original Xbox game without the emulator offers to open that section.
- Several versions of the system software can be installed side by side. System Software lists them with their sizes, with Use for Games and Remove for each, and Install from Files adds another version: a USB system update, or a Dashboard's own files (dash.xex and the files beside it).
- The library has a Dashboard tile for each installed version, and each Dashboard runs on its own system software. With Start with the Dashboard on, Settings → Startup chooses which version's Dashboard opens.
- XeniOS cleans up after itself at launch: temporary files older than a day, and copies Metal left behind while saving shaders, are removed. On one iPhone those copies had grown to 15 GB.
- The log file stops growing at 256 MB.
- Delete Profile, from the profile list or a profile's page. It removes the profile and its saves, achievements and settings from the device.
- Online profiles have two choices:
  - Delete from This Device removes the profile here and keeps the online account and gamertag. If no other device is signed in to the account, only its recovery code can bring it back.
  - Delete Account deletes the online account as well. The gamertag becomes free, and other devices signed in to it are signed out. This needs a connection to the online service. XeniOS keeps a record of the account's gamertag and its device and network identifiers, so a deleted account can still be banned.
- Delete Game, in a game page's menu, with options to also delete its updates, add-ons and saves. Deleting a game also removes its art and icons.

## Known issues

- One Halo 3 scene takes about 15% more frame time than before on a Mac. It adds light into a gamma render target, and that blending now runs in the shader to match the console.
- Original Xbox games are slow. Halo 2 ran at about 10 frames per second on an iPhone 17 before this version's recompiler change; we haven't measured it on a phone since.
- Live, online System Link, the Xbox 360 Dashboard and original Xbox games are experimental.

Fixes on top of 2.3.0.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Fixes

- When the app runs out of memory while compiling game code, it now says so instead of crashing without a message.
- Fixed the Achievements screen freezing the app on some devices.

XeniOS Live: an online account, friends, game invites, parties and party voice, through the XeniOS lobby at live.xenios.jp.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Live

- A profile can sign in to XeniOS Live with an online account kept by the XeniOS lobby. Your gamertag is checked for availability; another device joins the same account with a link code from a signed-in device, or with a recovery code, and a device that's already signed in approves new ones.
- Friends: add a friend with their friend code, a QR code, a shared link, or by searching their gamertag. Accept, decline and remove friends; see who's online, what they're playing, and your offline friends.
- Sharing your friend code sends a link to live.xenios.jp with your code and its QR code, which shows as a card in chats.
- Game invites: invite a friend from the in-game Online panel or from the game, and join from the invite banner. An invite accepted outside the game starts the game and joins the session; an invite to another game starts that game.
- Parties: start a party, invite anyone, and follow the party leader into their game. Parties have their own voice chat, separate from game chat.
- Matchmaking: games that search for Live sessions find the sessions other XeniOS players host, through the lobby.
- Stats and leaderboards are kept by the lobby.
- Voice chat is on by default, with a Microphone choice (Off, this device or a headset) in Settings > Online and the in-game menu.
- Block and report players, Appear Offline, and Recent Players. Blocked players are muted in games, and their sessions are hidden.
- Public Games lists the games other XeniOS players are in, without your own.
- Xbox 360 Dashboard: Friends and Party open the Online panel, and My Games lists your games.

## Settings

- Settings > Online: Private Rooms by Default for System Link, and the Microphone. A game's page shows its Online Room.

## Profiles

- Gamer pictures: choose one of the Xbox 360 gamer pictures for the signed-in profile (Profile page > Edit). They come from the Xbox 360 system software, so it has to be installed.
- A profile, with its account and saves, travels as one `.xeniosprofile` file; the Mac imports one from the Finder or AirDrop.

## In-game menu

- Quit Game: in a game started from the dashboard, choose Quit to Library or Quit to Dashboard.

## Tested

- Halo 3: game invites and parties between Mac instances; an iPhone joined a Mac Halo 3 lobby from an invite through the lobby.
- Halo 3 Mythic (4 players), Gears of War and Virtua Fighter 5 matchmade and played over System Link through the lobby.
- Party voice between a Mac and an iPhone, both ways.
- Friends, offline friends, Remove Friend, gamertag search and friend-code sharing on an iPhone.

## Known issues

- Live, online System Link and the Xbox 360 Dashboard are experimental.
- Players who take friend requests by code only can't be found by gamertag.

Fixes on top of 2.2.4.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## App

- When the JIT tool is attached but doesn't answer, XeniOS now says JIT isn't available instead of crashing.
- If quitting takes more than 4 seconds, XeniOS exits instead of waiting for iOS to end it.

## Known issues

- Online System Link and the Xbox 360 Dashboard are still experimental.

Fixes on top of 2.2.3.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Emulation

- Fixed a crash at game start or while saving shaders when memory is low: saved pipelines are skipped when there isn't room to load them, and compile as usual instead.
- Quitting or closing a game no longer waits for a pipeline save in progress or for a stalled GPU, which could make iOS end the app.

## App

- In games with local multiplayer, a second player's profile is signed in for that player instead of replacing the first player's.
- When the app runs out of memory, it now says so and names the likely cause instead of closing without a message.
- Compatibility data is checked for changes at most every 6 hours instead of downloaded in full at every launch.
- Game covers are no longer deleted after an app update for games the library hadn't finished loading yet.
- Long button titles on the System Software page wrap instead of being cut off.
- The Head Tracking switch is hidden on installs that can't use it.
- The first time a game looks for a network while System Link is off, XeniOS offers to turn System Link on in one tap, and the running game is told the network is now up. Some games, such as Black Ops 2, stop with an error without it.

## Known issues

- Online System Link and the Xbox 360 Dashboard are still experimental.

A fix on top of 2.2.2.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Emulation

- Fixed a GPU hang on the second and later launches of a game in 2.2.2, when its shaders were loaded from the new on-disk shader cache. Halo 3 hung on every launch after the first. Shaders already stored by 2.2.2 are kept and work again.

## Known issues

- Online System Link and the Xbox 360 Dashboard are still experimental.

Fixes and improvements on top of 2.2.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Emulation

- Translated shaders and compiled pipelines are now kept on disk between launches, so a game's stored shaders come back faster after a restart or an app update, when iOS has cleared its own shader cache. The first launch after updating to 2.2.1 builds the new cache.
- Draws that write to memory no longer stall the game while their shaders compile, as in upstream Xenia. What they write may show up a few frames late instead.
- GPU and CPU fixes: the GPU command thread sleeps instead of spinning a CPU core through long waits, does less work between command buffers, and some hot CPU loops run in fewer instructions. Texture uploads go through a staging buffer again, and depth state is fixed in passes without a depth buffer.
- Fixed "JIT code cache is full" right after launch on devices without TXM, such as M1 iPads.
- Quieter logs: per-draw GPU lines and disc file walks are logged only at debug level.

## App

- External displays: with a USB-C, HDMI or AirPlay display connected, the game fills that display at the right aspect ratio. The device keeps the touch controls and the in-game menu.
- The Library background is drawn from the art of the game it shows.
- While shaders are prepared before the first frame, the game is held and a note offers Play Now or Cancel after 8 seconds.
- If JIT is off when a game starts, XeniOS says how to turn it back on instead of failing with a fatal error.
- Online: the Online button counts the devices online, and the Online sheet is simpler. System Link says when your network blocks direct connections to another player.
- Fixed crashes: a title update mismatch warning, an unanswered JIT request, running out of address space for thread stacks, and shutdowns that hung past iOS's time limit.
- System Link messages no longer show wrong player counts, such as "Can't connect to 17,170,505 players".
- Cover art retries a dropped connection after 30 seconds instead of five minutes.

## Known issues

- Online System Link and the Xbox 360 Dashboard are still experimental.

First release since 2.0.1. It pulls in five months of [Xenia Edge](https://github.com/has207/xenia-edge) changes and reworks most of the app.

Many more games now render correctly and are playable than in 2.0.1. If a game didn't work for you before, try it again.

Requires iOS / iPadOS 26 or later. A Mac build for Apple Silicon (macOS 15 or later) is attached as well.

## Emulation

- Reworked Metal backend and faster ARM64 CPU emulation, with a long list of graphics, audio and kernel fixes from Xenia Edge.
- General performance and rendering improvements.
- Fixed a cause of crackling audio on iPhone.
- Audio comes back after calls, Siri, alarms and headphone changes.
- Shaders compile in the background and are cached for the next launch. The ones a game needs first are built first. A small indicator shows when shaders are compiling (Settings › Display to hide it).
- Games that launch another game, or another part of themselves, stay inside XeniOS.
- Multi-disc games: when a game asks for another disc, you pick it from that game's discs in your library.

## App

- New Library, game page, Settings, Profiles, Online screen, pause menu, touch layout editor and JIT setup sheet.
- Controller navigation everywhere: the Library, game pages, Settings, sheets and alerts.
- A launch screen replaces the black screen while a game starts. If a step hangs, a Cancel button appears.
- The in-game menu has a Pause Emulator button. Otherwise the game keeps running behind the menu, so System Link sessions don't stall. XeniOS still pauses when you leave the app, lock the device or take a call.
- Imports, add-ons and title updates copy in the background, with progress and a free-space check.
- The library shows instantly on launch and refreshes in the background.
- Linked folders survive renames, moves and remounts. Add-ons can be installed from them.
- Settings are searchable, save as you change them, and keep only what you changed. Reset All Settings keeps your signed-in profiles.
- A bigger default move stick. Saved touch layouts keep their old size.
- After a crash, XeniOS offers to share the log with your folder names stripped out.
- 120 Hz menus on ProMotion iPhones, Game Mode in games, and a warning when the device gets hot.
- VoiceOver works with the touch controls and most screens.
- Links from other apps that launch a game or read your library ask first.

## Experimental

Both of these are early. Expect bugs and please report them.

- Online System Link: play System Link games with other XeniOS players over the internet, in a game's public lobby or a private room you invite friends to. Tap Online in the library, or System Link in a game's menu. Everyone needs 2.2 and Online Features turned on. Players in a room can see each other's IP address and a profile ID.
- Xbox 360 Dashboard: tap its tile in the library and follow the one-page setup to download Microsoft's system update (about 116 MB). It installs on its own. You can start games in your library from the dashboard's disc tray.

## Privacy

- XeniOS can send anonymous crash reports and performance stats (frame rate, load times). No files, names or Apple Account. Turn it off in Settings › Privacy › Share Diagnostics. Details: [xenios.jp/privacy](https://xenios.jp/privacy#app-diagnostics).
- Turning off Online Features stops all of XeniOS's network requests: update checks, compatibility data, cover art, System Link and diagnostics.

## Known issues

- Online System Link and the Xbox 360 Dashboard are experimental.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: System Link uses your local network to play with other devices running XeniOS or Xenia, and with an XLink Kai engine on your network.
privacy.NSMotionUsageDescription: Head tracking adjusts spatial audio to your head movement when using the PHASE audio backend with supported headphones.

- With no network connection (for example in Airplane Mode), the app no longer tries to reach the online service. Online screens say "No Internet Connection", and everything reconnects by itself when the connection returns. Local play and System Link on your local network still work.
- A profile the online service has stopped (refused, removed, or signed in on another device) keeps showing the reason when the network returns, instead of trying again.
- The online service now gets a device ID that stays the same when the app is deleted and installed again: a hash of a random value kept in the Keychain, or on a Mac a hash of the hardware ID. Device bans rely on it.
- Anonymous crash reports and statistics that couldn't be sent because the network dropped are sent when it returns.
- While stored shaders are rebuilt, the launch screen and the in-game shader indicator show that rebuild's own progress from the start, and stop when it is done. Before, the bar could run ahead, jump, or stay on "Preparing shaders" until the first frame.
- Crash reports say where in the game's code a crash happened and what led up to it: the last few events (game start, first frame, memory warnings, going to the background, heat), the game's version, and which emulation settings differ from their defaults.
- Compatibility data is checked once a day instead of every six hours.
- Notice text on the library is easier to read, and the profile page is more compact.
- Converting the whole library to ZAR shows how much space it saved.
- Settings has a Startup page under App, with Start with the Dashboard and Turn On JIT Automatically. They were under Advanced → Automation. The Turn On JIT sheet has the same switch for opening StikDebug automatically.
- Live Log is a dark console: each line is marked in its level's colour, it can be filtered to warnings or errors, and a Latest button returns to the end.

## New

- Storage, under Settings → Library & Storage. It shows what XeniOS uses by kind and by game, and for each game offers Clear Shaders, Delete Updates and Add-ons, Delete Saves and Delete Game. Clear Game Data, Clear All Shaders and Clean Up Leftover Files work on the whole app. Files left by games that are no longer in the library are listed too.
- Storage also sorts games by size or name, deletes several selected games together, and deletes one disc of a game that has several. Games in a linked folder on the device are counted as Linked Games; games linked from another drive are listed outside the total.
- Original Xbox games are listed in the library with their cover and name, as disc images, ZAR archives or extracted folders, and start through the Xbox 360's own Xbox emulator. Storage lists them in their own section. Experimental and slow: see Known issues.
- XeniOS doesn't include that Xbox emulator. System Software has an Original Xbox Games section that installs it from Files (the Compatibility folder from an Xbox 360's hard drive, the folder it is in, or its files), shows what is installed, and removes it. Start Games With chooses the build games start through: Automatic, where xbox.xex picks one for each game as the console does, or any installed build. A game's own Game Settings has Xbox Emulator Build to choose a different one for that game. Opening an original Xbox game without the emulator offers to open that section.
- Several versions of the system software can be installed side by side. System Software lists them with their sizes, with Use for Games and Remove for each, and Install from Files adds another version: a USB system update, or a Dashboard's own files (dash.xex and the files beside it).
- The library has a Dashboard tile for each installed version, and each Dashboard runs on its own system software. With Start with the Dashboard on, Settings → Startup chooses which version's Dashboard opens.
- XeniOS cleans up after itself at launch: temporary files older than a day, and copies Metal left behind while saving shaders, are removed. On one iPhone those copies had grown to 15 GB.
- The log file stops growing at 256 MB.
- Delete Profile, from the profile list or a profile's page. It removes the profile and its saves, achievements and settings from the device.
- Online profiles have two choices:
  - Delete from This Device removes the profile here and keeps the online account and gamertag. If no other device is signed in to the account, only its recovery code can bring it back.
  - Delete Account deletes the online account as well. The gamertag becomes free, and other devices signed in to it are signed out. This needs a connection to the online service. XeniOS keeps a record of the account's gamertag and its device and network identifiers, so a deleted account can still be banned.
- Delete Game, in a game page's menu, with options to also delete its updates, add-ons and saves. Deleting a game also removes its art and icons.

## Known issues

- One Halo 3 scene takes about 15% more frame time than before on a Mac. It adds light into a gamma render target, and that blending now runs in the shader to match the console.
- Original Xbox games are slow. Halo 2 ran at about 10 frames per second on an iPhone 17 before this version's recompiler change; we haven't measured it on a phone since.
- Live, online System Link, the Xbox 360 Dashboard and original Xbox games are experimental.
